meta.title: RacePlan — a safe training plan for your next race
meta.description: Free, personalized training plans for amateur runners, from 5K to marathon and trail.
meta.newPlanDescription: Answer a few questions about your race and your running and get a free, week-by-week training plan with paces.

header.theme: Theme: {theme, select, light {light} dark {dark} other {system}}. Change theme

footer.privacy: Your data never leaves your browser.
footer.madeWith: Plans are generated by transparent, rules-based coaching logic — no AI.

landing.title: RacePlan
landing.headline: A safe, personalized training plan for your next race
landing.subtitle: Tell us about your race and your running. Get a clear week-by-week calendar with paces, built on proven coaching rules — from 5K to marathon and trail.

features.safeBody: Gradual volume increases, cutback weeks, rest days and a proper taper — always within the limits you set.
features.personalBody: Your race, your current fitness, your available days and your injury history shape every week.
features.exportBody: Read it on your phone, switch km/miles, and export the whole plan to PDF.

landing.how2: Get your plan: phases, weekly volume, paces and every workout.
landing.how3: Follow it week by week — tap any day for details.

form.title: Create your plan

stepIntro.race: Which race are you preparing for?
stepIntro.fitness: All optional — they help us set your paces. Without them, you'll train by effort.
stepIntro.training: Your recent running and how much time you have.
stepIntro.health: This keeps the plan safe for you.
stepIntro.style: How do you like to train?

form.draftRestored: We restored your answers from last time.

distance.label: Race distance

prDate.label: When did you run it?

yearsRunning.label: How long have you been running?

availableDays.label: Days you can run

planStyle.label: Plan style
planStyle.balancedDesc: A varied mix of threshold, intervals, hills and race-pace work. Recommended for most runners.
planStyle.vdotDesc: Structured, pace-driven sessions in the style of Jack Daniels' training zones.
planStyle.polarizedDesc: At least 80% very easy running, with a few genuinely hard sessions.

preferences.label: Workout preferences
preferences.hint: We'll swap disliked workouts for ones with a similar effect.

plan.title: Your training plan
plan.disclaimer: This plan is general guidance, not medical advice. See a doctor before starting if you have any health concerns. Stop and rest if pain persists.
plan.optionalNote: This session is optional — skip it if you feel tired.
plan.crossTraining: Optional: swap this run for 30–45 minutes of low-impact cross-training (cycling, swimming, elliptical) if your legs need a break.
plan.effortOnlyIntro: Without a recent race time, you'll train by feel. Use these effort levels; the time trial in the first weeks shows you where you stand.
plan.daysToGo: {count, plural, one {# day to go} other {# days to go}}

timeTrial.intro: Enter your {distance} time to get personal paces for the rest of your plan.
timeTrial.keepsPast: Weeks that have already started stay as they are.

errors.implausible_time: That time doesn't look right for this distance.

plan.zonesFromTimeTrial: Paces from your time trial: {distance} in {time} ({date}).

longProgressive.title: Long run with a {fastM} steady finish

longRacePace.title: Long run with {rpM} at race pace

note.raceDay: Warm up with 10–15 minutes of easy jogging and a few strides. Start conservatively and enjoy it!
note.timeTrial: Run it as a hard, even effort on a flat route. Note your time — it tells you your current fitness.
note.hillSprints: Very short, powerful uphill efforts on a steep slope. Walk or jog back down slowly and recover fully.
note.hillRepeats: Run uphill at a strong, controlled effort. Jog back down easily.
note.fartlek: Play with speed: the hard parts are by feel, no need to look at your watch.
note.shakeout: Just 15–20 minutes very easy to loosen up — or rest if you prefer.
note.trailLong: Time on feet matters more than distance: aim for about {gainM} of climbing on hilly trails. The distance shown is a flat-road estimate.
note.powerHike: Power-hike the steep climbs — most trail runners do on race day too.
note.downhill: Quick, short steps, eyes ahead, relaxed arms. Stop if your knees complain.

trailLong.title: Trail long run: {seconds} on your feet

recovery.label: Very easy
recovery.desc: Slower than easy — just loosening up. Breathing fully relaxed.

easy.label: Easy
easy.desc: Conversational: you can talk in full sentences. Most of your running.

steady.label: Steady
steady.desc: Comfortably brisk: you can still talk in short sentences.

marathon.label: Marathon effort
marathon.desc: Controlled and sustainable for a long time; talking in short phrases.

threshold.label: Comfortably hard
threshold.desc: You could hold it for about an hour; only a few words at a time.

interval.label: Hard
interval.desc: Strong effort you could sustain for 10–15 minutes; talking is difficult.

repetition.label: Fast and relaxed
repetition.desc: Quick, smooth and controlled — not a sprint. Full recovery between.

race.label: Race effort
race.desc: The effort you plan to hold on race day.

powerHike.label: Power hike
powerHike.desc: Brisk uphill walking with purpose, hands on knees if steep.

warning.plan_too_short: Your race is in {weeks} weeks; we recommend at least {minWeeks}. The plan is compressed, without catching-up jumps in volume.
warning.goal_ambitious: Your goal implies a {gainPct}% fitness gain (realistic: up to {limitPct}%). Your paces are based on your current fitness.
warning.low_max_volume: Your maximum of {maxM} per week is low for this race (we'd suggest about {suggestedM}). Consider a shorter race or be very cautious.
warning.few_days_available: Running only {days} days a week is little for this distance. The plan stays safe but may feel limited.
warning.no_performance_data: No recent race time: you'll train by effort. Try the optional time trial early on.
warning.old_pr: Your personal record is {months} months old, so we've adjusted it to be more conservative.
warning.preference_unmet: We couldn't avoid every "{tag}" session without losing an important training effect.
warning.minor_runner: You're under 18: volumes are capped. Please train with a coach or a parent involved.
warning.risk_flagged: For your safety, the plan is more conservative ({flags}).
warning.race_ready_mini_plan: Your race is very close: this is a short race-ready plan — maintain, sharpen, rest.
warning.max_below_current: Your maximum is below your current volume, so the plan starts at your maximum.
warning.long_base_block: Your race is far away: the first {weeks} weeks are an easy base-maintenance block before the 24-week plan.
warning.long_break: You've been away for more than 4 weeks ({days} days). Your fitness has changed: update your answers to get a plan that matches your running now.
warning.goal_reassess: Because of the missed training, your biggest week is now lower than planned, so your target time may be out of reach. Run by effort and check it again after a race or time trial.

advice.softSurfaces: With your shin/bone history, run on softer surfaces (trails, grass, track) when you can, and keep easy runs truly easy.
advice.cadence: For knee / IT band history, keep a slightly quicker, shorter stride and avoid long downhills.
advice.achilles: For your Achilles/calf, hill sprints and very fast running are avoided in the first third of the plan. Warm up well.
advice.plantar: With plantar fasciitis history, hills and speed work never appear in the same week.
advice.crossTraining: Cross-training (cycling, swimming) can replace an easy run whenever you need a lower-impact day.
advice.recovery50: After each long run you get at least two easy or rest days before the next hard session.
advice.minor: Growing bodies need recovery: sleep well, eat enough, and tell an adult or coach about any pain.
advice.effortOnly: Effort descriptions replace paces. The talk test is your best guide.

log.title: How did it go?
log.hint: Not marked = done as planned. Your plan adapts from next Monday.
log.error: Sorry, this couldn't be saved. Please try again.

adapt.title: Adapted to your log
adapt.hold: You missed part of last week, so this week stays at {distanceM} instead of increasing.
adapt.cutback: Two weeks in a row with missed runs: this is now a lighter recovery week.
adapt.easyOnly: Easy running only again this week, to rebuild after your break.

break.short: Welcome back after {days} days off: your first 2 runs are easy and the volume doesn't increase this week.
break.medium: After {days} days off, this week restarts at about 75% of your last level, with easy running and strides only.
break.long: After {days} days off, this week restarts at about half your last level, with easy running only for 2 weeks and paces 3% slower.
break.veryLong: After {days} days off, this week restarts at about half your last level, with easy running only for 2 weeks and paces 3% slower. Your plan may no longer fit: update your answers.
break.shortBack: After your {days} days off, the volume doesn't increase this week.

adapt.fatigue: You felt tired last week, so the volume doesn't increase this week and one hard session is now an easy run.
adapt.fatigueCutback: Two tiring weeks in a row: this is now a lighter recovery week.
adapt.pain: Because of your pain, the 7 days after your check-in are easy running only, about 20% shorter. Stop if the pain changes the way you run, and see a health professional if it lasts more than a week.
adapt.sick: You're ill: no running is planned until you tell us you're back. Don't run with a fever or chest symptoms.
adapt.injured: Plan paused because of your injury. See a health professional, and tell us when you can run again.
adapt.back: Welcome back after {days} days off: your runs this week are easy.

backup.body: Your plan and what you've logged are kept only in this browser. Save a backup file to keep them safe or to move them to another device.
backup.confirmReplace: Replace your current plan with the one in this file?

errors.invalid_file: This file isn't a valid RacePlan backup.
errors.unsupported_version: This backup comes from a different version of RacePlan and can't be loaded.

checkIn.title: How do you feel?
checkIn.hint: Your plan changes from tomorrow. For today's workout, mark it yourself if you don't run.

noted.tired: Noted: you feel tired or sore. Next week won't increase and has one hard session less.
noted.pain: Noted: pain or niggle. The next 7 days are easy and shorter.
noted.back: Welcome back! Your plan starts again gently.

paused.sick: Since {date}, because you're ill. Don't run with a fever or chest symptoms. Rest, and come back when you feel well.
paused.injured: Since {date}, because of an injury. See a health professional before running again.

checkIn.backHint: Your plan restarts gently from today, depending on how long you were away.

raceGuide.hubIntro: Free, personalised plans for some of the world's biggest marathons. Pick your race to see what the course asks of you, your training calendar and sample plans computed for the next edition. Then create your own in a few minutes.
raceGuide.hubMetaDescription: Free training plans for the world's biggest marathons: course notes, training calendar, sample plans computed for each race, then your personalised plan.
raceGuide.title: {name} {year} training plan
raceGuide.metaDescription: {summary} Sample plans from {minWeeks} to {maxWeeks} weeks computed for the {year} edition, then your free personalised plan.
raceGuide.independent: Independent page: RacePlan has no connection with the organisers of this race. Check the date, course and registration on the official website.
raceGuide.ctaBody: The form is pre-filled with the race and its date: add your level and availability, and your week-by-week plan is ready. Free, no account, your data stays in your browser.
raceGuide.courseTitle: What this course asks of you
raceGuide.samplesIntro: Three typical runners, planned by RacePlan for the {year} edition. Your plan will depend on your answers: it's a starting point, not a plan to copy.
raceGuide.samplesEstimated: As the date isn't announced yet, these samples use {date} as a reference.
raceGuide.faqStartQ: When should I start training for the {name} {year}?
raceGuide.faqStartA: Count back from race day: {list}. The earlier you start, the gentler the build-up can be.
raceGuide.faqVolumeQ: How many kilometres a week to train for the {name}?
raceGuide.faqVolumeA: In our samples, the biggest week ranges from {minPeak} to {maxPeak}, with a longest run from {minLong} to {maxLong}. It all depends on what you run today: RacePlan starts from your current volume, increases it by at most 10% a week and plans a lighter week every 3 to 4 weeks.
raceGuide.notChecked: Information from public sources: confirm it on the race's official website.
raceGuide.faqStartEstimated: The {year} date isn't announced yet. Using {date} as a reference: {list}. Recalculate once the official date is known.
